participants.name: Maria Gonzalez
participants.professional_persona: Senior Tax Compliance Officer at the IRS with 12 years of experience in administering refundable credits. She leads the team developing the Non-Filer Sign-Up Tool and oversees outreach to low-income families.
participants.skills_and_expertise: Expert in tax law interpretation and IT system requirements for benefit delivery. Skilled in stakeholder coordination and multilingual community engagement.
participants.career_goals_and_ambitions: Aims to become Director of Taxpayer Services and expand IRS digital tools to reduce filing barriers for underserved populations.

policy_role_context.role_label: IRS Child Tax Credit implementation official
objectives: Administer advance Child Tax Credit eligibility, payment calculations, taxpayer updates, and reconciliation accurately.
constraints: Must operate within statutory authority, administrative capacity, data quality, identity-verification, and notice requirements.
actions: IRS implements the advance payment program under new section 7527A.
IRS evaluates taxpayer eligibility based on return data.
IRS uses portal information to adjust payment amounts.

participants.name: Marlene K. Ashford
participants.occupation: Deputy Assistant Secretary for Fiscal Operations
participants.professional_persona: Marlene is a Deputy Assistant Secretary for Fiscal Operations and Policy at the Treasury Department, overseeing the disbursement of funds for the Child Tax Credit expansion. She has spent the last decade managing large-scale federal assistance programs, ensuring compliance with appropriations law and Treasury oversight.
participants.skills_and_expertise: Expert in federal budget execution, grant management, and interagency coordination; skilled in designing fiscal controls for high-volume payment programs.
participants.career_goals_and_ambitions: She aims to streamline Treasury's fiscal service delivery for social programs and eventually lead the Office of Management and Budget's financial management division.

objectives: Execute advance payment batches reliably and ensure funds reach eligible households on schedule.
constraints: Must translate IRS payment instructions into high-volume disbursements under operational, timing, and data constraints.
actions: Bureau of the Fiscal Service receives funds to carry out the advance payment program.
Bureau of the Fiscal Service carries out fiscal services for the advance payment program.
Treasury appropriates $16,200,000 to Bureau of the Fiscal Service for carrying out the advance payment section.

participants.name: James Thompson
participants.professional_persona: James is a married father of three working as an electrician in suburban Ohio. He and his wife both work full-time, and the Child Tax Credit helps them pay for after-school programs and summer camps.
participants.skills_and_expertise: Licensed electrician with expertise in residential and commercial wiring, and skilled in financial planning for his family.
participants.career_goals_and_ambitions: James aims to start his own electrical contracting business within five years to build generational wealth for his children.

policy_role_context.role_label: Parent automatically receiving advance Child Tax Credit payments
objectives: Receive the correct advance credit on time and use the added income to meet household and child needs.
constraints: Must manage household changes, payment accuracy, and possible year-end reconciliation with limited control over program administration.
actions: Most eligible families automatically receive monthly Child Tax Credit payments.
Eligible families automatically receive monthly advance Child Tax Credit payments.
Most families in the U.S. automatically receive advance monthly Child Tax Credit payments.

participants.name: Linda Chen
participants.professional_persona: Linda is a recent immigrant and works part-time as a restaurant server while caring for her two school-age children. She has never filed a U.S. tax return and relies on community organizations for support.
participants.skills_and_expertise: She is bilingual in Mandarin and English and is adept at customer service, but is unfamiliar with the U.S. tax system and online IRS tools.
participants.career_goals_and_ambitions: Linda aspires to become a certified interpreter or translator, and she wants to ensure her children have opportunities for higher education.

objectives: Learn about eligibility, complete registration, and receive the full credit despite not normally filing a tax return.
constraints: May face information, documentation, identity-verification, language, digital-access, and institutional-trust barriers.
actions: Non-filer household must use the Non-Filer Sign-up Tool to register for advance payments.
Non-filer household receives advance Child Tax Credit payments after registration.
Non-filer household with qualifying child is eligible for the refundable credit if they meet residency requirements.

participants.name: James Thompson
participants.professional_persona: James is a tax preparer and financial coach at a Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) site in rural Mississippi. He works directly with low-income families and seniors, helping them file taxes and claim credits like the Child Tax Credit. His calm demeanor and patience make him a trusted figure in his community.
participants.skills_and_expertise: Certified tax preparer with deep knowledge of IRS forms and eligibility rules. He excels at using IRS online tools to help clients check their advance payment status and resolve issues.
participants.career_goals_and_ambitions: James wants to open his own community tax center to provide year-round financial literacy services. He hopes to train other volunteers to expand outreach across the Delta region.

constraints: Must work with limited outreach capacity, uneven community trust, language needs, and changing federal guidance.
